per_policy_guidance.guidance: Observed reliability: 3/12 final-state successes (25%) from this policy’s own replay-reached training-segment entries. The three successes first reached the task predicate at rollout steps 240–293; in all nine failures blue remained at goal but red was not at goal. No run had an unconverged IK step, so IK convergence alone did not distinguish success. Do not use as the routine in-distribution choice. Its object-equivariant representation is designed for a reachable displaced or yawed red source, but that benefit was not validated out of distribution; consider it only as a closely monitored, structurally matched fallback when such source variation dominates and stronger validated alternatives are unsuitable. Enter only with blue descending to or settled in blue_goal, red observable/reachable in the central free area, and finite robot/object state. Avoid unstable blue, noisy or unreachable targets, obstacles, ambiguous nearest-object selection, missed attachment, or slip. Recognize failure if the reference selector oscillates, red does not rise after closure, red separates in transport, release misses full goal containment, either block is disturbed on retreat, or the final predicate remains false—especially the validated pattern blue_at_goal=true/red_at_goal=false. Terminal handoff: there is no successor; stop only when both red_at_goal and blue_at_goal are observed. Gripper sign, reference identity, open fingers, or a high retreat is not by itself success evidence.

Observed reliability: 12/12 final-state successes (100%) from its own in-distribution replay entries; first task success occurred at rollout steps 308–379. Every validation run had three gripper changes and zero unconverged IK steps. Use when blue is low over or settled in blue_goal, red is visible in the central buffer, and state is finite; it is a strong in-distribution choice for the complete terminal segment. The destination-anchored prior is designed to suit reachable red_goal translation and placement drift, especially after red is lifted, but translated-goal success was not tested. Avoid treating it as evidence for displaced-source pickup, missed grasp, slip, unstable blue, collisions, or unreachable goal geometry. Recognize failure if red does not track the TCP after closure, destination-relative IK residuals/limits persist, release occurs without full goal containment, blue leaves its goal, or either task predicate is false. Terminal handoff: no successor exists; continue or replan only until both red_at_goal and blue_at_goal are observed, then stop. Apparent lift, gripper sign, open fingers, or retreat posture alone is insufficient.

Observed reliability: 12/12 final-state successes (100%) from its own in-distribution replay entries, with the tightest observed first-success range, rollout steps 327–350. All runs had three gripper changes and zero unconverged IK steps. This is a strong conservative default when blue is low over/supported in blue_goal, red is observable, robot/scene values are finite, and the handoff phase or TCP configuration varies within the demonstrated range. Its fresh-TCP residual is intended to recenter moderate tracking/configuration mismatch, but no unseen-error recovery was validated. Avoid gross phase/configuration mismatch, large source or destination displacement as the dominant variation, unstable blue, missed contact, slip, obstacles, unreachable geometry, or relying on it to correct accumulated long-transport error. Recognize failure when repeated local targets make no progress, IK residuals or joint-limit contacts persist, red fails to lift or slips, release misses full containment, blue is displaced, or retreat contacts an object. Terminal handoff: no successor; stop only on the conjunction red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal. Small residuals, gripper state, open fingers, and high retreat are not completion predicates.

Observed reliability: 12/12 final-state successes (100%) from its own in-distribution replay entries; first success ranged from rollout step 282 to 575, making completion timing more variable than h02/h03. Every run had three gripper changes and zero unconverged IK steps. Use when blue is descending to or stable in blue_goal and red is observable, table-supported in the central buffer; the documented strongest case is after blue stabilizes and before red pickup, with red outside the 0.12 m horizontal red_goal switch radius and a conventional lift. Its phase-local anchors are designed for reachable translated red sources while switching to destination anchoring after lift, but source-translation generalization was not validated. Avoid an already-near-goal source, unusual low carry, slip, pose noise near anchor thresholds, changed nearest-object ordering, yaw-dominant variation, unstable blue, obstacles, or unreachable IK. Recognize failure through motion tied to blue/red/red_goal in the wrong phase, missed pickup, red remaining in the buffer, a low/slipping red causing the wrong switch, release outside full containment, more/oscillatory gripper changes versus the three seen in validation, blue displacement, or nonzero IK residuals/limit contacts. Terminal handoff: no successor; stop only when both goal predicates are observed, not on anchor identity, object height, closure, opening, or retreat alone.

summary: Validation was strictly in distribution: each policy started from the entry state of its own training segment in each of 12 demonstrations, reached by exact action replay, ran for 1.5× segment length, and was scored at the final state by the unchanged predicate red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal. There is no out-of-distribution or unseen-error-recovery evidence. For matching entries, h02, h03, and h04 each achieved 12/12; h03 had the narrowest first-success window (327–350), h02 was also consistent (308–379), and h04 was successful but more variable (282–575). A reasonable selection order is h03 as the conservative in-distribution default, h02 when destination anchoring is the relevant structural prior, and h04 when phase-local source-translation anchoring is relevant. Those latter specialization claims are representation-based expectations, not validated OOD outcomes. De-prioritize h01: it achieved only 3/12, with all nine failures preserving blue_at_goal but missing red_at_goal despite no unconverged IK. All four skills are terminal and have no successor; the runtime agent should declare handoff/completion only after observing both goal predicates and should otherwise stop, replan, or select another applicable policy based on the listed failure signatures.
